title: Running a protocol and a reached subprotocol agree
statement: Let $p$ and $s$ be deterministic two-party communication protocols over Alice's input type $X$ and Bob's input type $Y$ with output type $\alpha$, and let $\pi$ be a subprotocol path witnessing that $s$ sits at a rooted subtree of $p$. Suppose the input pair $(x, y)$ reaches $s$ along $\pi$, meaning $x$ lies in the set of Alice inputs consistent with all of Alice's branching choices on $\pi$ and $y$ lies in the set of Bob inputs consistent with all of Bob's branching choices on $\pi$. Then executing $p$ and executing $s$ on $(x, y)$ yield the same output.
hypotheses_covered: p and s are protocols over X, Y with output type α
a subprotocol path π witnesses s is a rooted subtree of p
(x, y) reaches s along π: x is consistent with Alice's choices and y with Bob's choices on π
replaced:
If the input pair $(x, y)$ reaches the subprotocol $s$ of $p$ via path \texttt{hsp}, then
running $p$ and running $s$ on $(x, y)$ produce the same output: $p.\texttt{run}\;x\;y =
s.\texttt{run}\;x\;y$.
